definitions.explanation: The act or moment of waking from sleep. Can describe the quality of how one wakes up.
A figurative awakening — becoming aware of something new, developing a new consciousness or interest.

examples.japanese: {今朝|けさ}は{目覚|めざ}めがよかった。
examples.english: I woke up feeling refreshed this morning.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}の{目覚|めざ}めとともに{花|はな}が{咲|さ}き{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: Flowers began to bloom with the awakening of spring.

examples.japanese: コーヒーの{香|かお}りで{心地|ここち}よい{目覚|めざ}めを{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: I had a pleasant awakening to the aroma of coffee.

examples.japanese: {芸術|げいじゅつ}への{目覚|めざ}め。
あの{旅|たび}が{自然|しぜん}への{目覚|めざ}めのきっかけだった。
examples.english: That trip was what sparked my awakening to nature.

examples.japanese: {十代|じゅうだい}の{頃|ころ}に{政治|せいじ}への{目覚|めざ}めを{経験|けいけん}し、{活動|かつどう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: I experienced a political awakening in my teens and started getting involved.

notes:
USAGE:
The nominal form of the verb {目覚|めざ}める (to wake up, to awaken). In sense 1, often used with adjectives describing how one wakes up: {目覚|めざ}めがいい (wakes up well), {目覚|めざ}めが{悪|わる}い (wakes up poorly). In sense 2, the pattern ～への{目覚|めざ}め (awakening to ~) is very common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目覚|めざ}めがいい: to wake up feeling good
- {目覚|めざ}めが{悪|わる}い: to wake up feeling groggy
- ～への{目覚|めざ}め: awakening to ~
- {目覚|めざ}めを{迎|むか}える: to experience an awakening
